answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock a refundable bond before receiving work, while randomly assigning agents to audit results against hidden test cases. A Sybil cluster that boosts its own ratings eventually fails a test, and a fraud proof slashes the bond; honest agents recover theirs after a delay. The attacker must therefore lock capital for every fake identity and risk losing it repeatedly, making mass imitation costly rather than hollow. Even if one fake slips through like a marble, scaling identities across the horizon remains expensive.
